principles: Do not optimize for the sake of optimization.
Preserve consistency between proof semantics, claim boundaries, and audit finding state.
drivers: F-009 is a suspected audit finding, so closure must be evidence-backed rather than cosmetic.
Layer2 Engineering proof must remain distinct from Layer4 Production Safety and Authority/customerKeyRef scope.
Lattice CLI must be the mutation path for story and finding state.

options.name: A: Resolve F-009 as stale/disproven if current formal proof path already covers the original claim
pros: Avoids implementing fake Authority or broad Layer4 behavior.
Removes a vague high/suspected advisory if it no longer describes current code.
cons: Requires strong source, doc, and command evidence to avoid false closure.

options.name: B: Narrow F-009 to a precise remaining Layer4 or Authority gap
pros: Preserves audit pressure if a concrete correctness gap remains.
Avoids closing a finding when only part of it is addressed.
cons: Could duplicate the already separate customerKeyRef Layer4 future-scope gap if applied too broadly.

options.name: C: Implement new proof/evaluator behavior inside this story
pros: Could address a real missing path if evidence shows the current path is absent or bypassable.
cons: Out of scope unless the audit proves a real correctness issue; risks arbitrary optimization and Layer4 scope creep.

chosen: A: Resolve F-009 as stale/disproven if current formal proof path already covers the original claim
rationale: Current evidence points to the original F-009 claim being outdated by the formal Layer2 proof path; the safest path is to resolve only that finding if verification confirms the proof path and higher-layer locks.

preMortem.scenario: F-009 is closed even though the formal path can still be bypassed by local-only artifacts.
preMortem.trigger: We rely on docs wording without checking source fail-closed checks.
preMortem.consequence: Layer2 could be falsely claimed from diagnostic evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Verify source checks for localOnly=false, capabilityProof=true, formal suite rebuild, and claim boundary locks before resolving.

preMortem.scenario: The story drifts into implementing Layer4 customerKeyRef or Authority receipts.
preMortem.trigger: Remaining gap_analyze high output is mistaken for the same F-009 issue.
preMortem.consequence: Scope creep consumes tokens and risks fake production authority semantics.
preMortem.mitigation: Treat customerKeyRef as separate Layer4 future/blocked scope unless explicitly implementing Layer4.

preMortem.trigger: We conflate formal proof path existence with current production-grade or global claim readiness.
preMortem.consequence: Audit state becomes inconsistent with capability claim boundaries.
preMortem.mitigation: Resolution wording must say only the original F-009 suspected gap is resolved/disproven and that Production/global claims remain locked.
